locator: I q.48 a.2 ad 2: et hoc modo etiam malum dicitur ens
interpretation: Aquinas distinguishes being as the entity of a thing (in which sense no privation is a being) from being as the truth of a proposition, answering the question 'an est' (in which sense blindness is in the eye and evil 'is'). Read as: when a privation is in a subject, the proposition that there is evil is true. Only this direction is formalized. Aquinas' account implies that the evil premise is truth-apt and that a privation, not anyone's attitude, fixes its truth. This reading does not formalize either point. It states only the conditional.
